phase: the data volume: eleven attempts, one assumption disproved, one route left
result: STOPPED BY DECISION, not by a wall

the_one_that_worked.what: a 439-second boot that came back cleanly, iOS home screen running at 10 fps
the_one_that_worked.what_it_proves: registering the data volume device does not disturb anything
the_one_that_worked.what_it_does_not_prove: that reading it works: zone_read was called zero times. The rc that boot ran was 'exec /sbin/launchd.ios' and nothing else.
the_one_that_worked.how_it_was_missed: it looked like a success, so the investigation stayed on the read path instead of asking what that boot had actually exercised

assumption_disproved.assumption: the APFS volume being mounted on the same device is what conflicts
assumption_disproved.experiment: unmount /redwood/lib first, then read flash block 608512
assumption_disproved.conclusion: the conflict is not between two users of the controller

two_real_bugs_fixed.what: d_psize returned a block count where a sector size is expected
two_real_bugs_fixed.detail: set_blocksize() stores it in v_specsize; spec_read rejects anything over PAGE_SIZE
two_real_bugs_fixed.reference: memdev's mdevsize and virtio_blk's blk_dev_size both return 512

two_real_bugs_fixed.what: one failed request poisoned the lease for good
two_real_bugs_fixed.detail: every failure called us_poison, including ones where nothing was issued; and the kernel's init refuses to run at all once state is not UR_UNUSED, so the first failure was permanent
two_real_bugs_fixed.fix: twoblock_refuse (gives the lease back, does not poison) versus twoblock_fail (both)

diagnostics_added.lease_state_on_the_screen: ufs-read guard: lease magic=... version=... trial=... state=0x3
diagnostics_added.guard_no_longer_spins: it used to loop on wfe before the kernel log was written, which is why ten failures produced no log at all

route_found_not_finished.how_it_differs: the kernel does not touch the UFS controller. It writes a request into a shared page and core 0 (the loader) does the read, flushes, and reads it back before answering.
route_found_not_finished.why_it_matters: it never enters the lease state machine, so it cannot poison it
route_found_not_finished.status: compiled into the kernel this round (bsd/conf/files: optional -> standard, and the empty versions in hakios.stubs.c turned off)
route_found_not_finished.what_is_missing: the kernel wants boot-arg ufs_shared_pa and the loader does not supply one. The loader needs to set aside a shared page, pass its address, and service requests on core 0.

process_failure: eleven flips, each confirmed by flashing. Two bugs were found by reading the source, none by testing. Worse: the one clean boot was never pinned as a baseline, so the reproducible success was lost by continuing to edit.
